defects.summary: After an in-task interactive card (gate card or completion card) resolved on the NO-OVERLAY path, the loop never returned Chrome to the foreground: post-approval EXECUTE failed (dispatchGesture cannot land in a background app) and OBSERVE read 0 lines (foreground window = harness) -> spurious REFUSED. Overlay path unaffected; 08J completion-card path unaffected (task ends at the card).

navigator_accessibility_service_config.xml lacked android:canRequestEnhancedWebAccessibility and filtered packageNames to com.android.chrome only, so the AVD's org.chromium.webview_shell delivered toolbar-only trees (pageNodes=2) to the bound service. Real Chrome ignores the capability: additive and safe.

fixes.mechanism: New HarnessFrontAware (both Debug presenters report shouldBringToFront per presentation). The loop, right after each interactive resolution, re-fronts the browser BEFORE the loop continues when the presenter fronted the harness: VIEW intent for GateCard.url (completion card: current obs.url; only real http(s) URLs fire) through the existing cold-start BrowserLauncher seam + Config.restoreSettleMs (default 1000ms), logged on the step log; openBrowser logs every VIEW intent on NavigatorHarness. Excluded: task-ending resolutions (DENY-abort, CONFIRM_DONE), overlay-path and never-fronting (scripted/auto) presentations, trusted no-card actions, non-page URLs — all byte-identical no-ops. 30s timeouts, once-per-task completion card, and card payloads untouched.

Added android:canRequestEnhancedWebAccessibility="true"; widened android:packageNames to the manifest's two allowlisted browsers com.android.chrome,org.chromium.webview_shell; comment updated (code-side PACKAGE_ALLOWLIST stays authoritative). No touch-exploration capability (owner-directed trade).

deviations.deviation: Dispatch specified the packageNames separator as a pipe; shipped a COMMA.
deviations.reason: The platform parses android:packageNames as a comma-separated list (AccessibilityManagerService.parseServiceInfo splits on \s*,\s*); a pipe would form one non-matching package name and kill event delivery for BOTH browsers.
